summary: Sarah Harding is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche in 1972 and Drubpon Lama Tenpa from around 1976 to 1980. She held posts at Naropa University (~1992–2018) and the Tsadra Foundation (~2009).

Sarah J. Horton specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).

Sarah Shaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. Her Oxford affiliations include Wolfson College, the Faculty of Oriental Studies, and an honorary fellowship at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies (attested 2013).
Saraju Rath is a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. She held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1906–1980) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea. He served as a librarian at The Asiatic Society and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. He studied at Presidency College, Chennai, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, and trained under Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Pelden Chophel. He directed the Bhutia Boarding School and translated for Bengal.

Sarat Sarma is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Manipur University under the supervision of S. Shyamkishor Singh, also studying under S. Lokendrajit Singh (attested 2006).
Saroja Bhate (born 1942) is an Indologist and linguist. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 2000 and 2011.
Sarva Daman Singh is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served on the faculty at the University of Queensland, including as Professor of History (attested 1958 and 1987).

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian who studied at Madras Christian College, Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras (~1940–1944), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1945–1951). He later held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1971–1983).

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Madras Christian College. He held professorships at the universities of Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University and Banaras Hindu University, and Chancellor of the University of Delhi.

Saswati Mutsuddy is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Dipak Kumar Barua. She served on the teaching staff in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).

Satiranjan Sen was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied at Peking University. He held positions as a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.
Satish Chandra (1922–2017) was a historian and Indologist. He studied at the University of Allahabad (~1940–1948) and held a post as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University (~1953–1961).

Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Krishnagar Government College, Sanskrit College, and Calcutta University under Sarat Chandra Das. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at Presidency University and The Asiatic Society.

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1948–1955) and became the second director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.

Satoru Harada (born 1947) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo (~1971–1974) and held posts at the Toyo Bunko (attested 1978), the Eastern Institute (attested 1982), and Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).

Satoru Noriyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Esho Mikogami (attested 1996). He has held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003, 2013).
Satoshi Hayashima is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2013) and later served as a lecturer there (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan, working under Shozen Kumoi, Takao Kagawa, and Luis O. Gómez. He later served as a professor and president at Kyoto Bunkyo University.
